anatomy.intro: Follow one complete compound leaf from its separate blades to the stalk that joins the branch.

parts.function: The broad blade catches light; its side veins loop together inside the margin.
parts.label: Leaflet blade

parts.function: Several leaflets meet at one point, forming the hand-shaped leaf.
parts.label: Leaflet junction

parts.function: The long leaf stalk holds the entire compound leaf away from the trunk.
parts.label: Petiole

parts.function: The upright woody axis supports the canopy as the tree develops.
parts.label: Trunk

flowers.text: Pachira glabra bears pale green to whitish flowers in leaf axils. Narrow petals curl backward, exposing a brush of long stamens. The smooth, egg-shaped capsule contains many large seeds.

growth.note: Watch shoot tips for unfolding leaflets and follow the shared stalk to distinguish a new leaf from a new branch. NParks describes the species as fast-growing.

stages.text: Young shoots carry developing compound leaves whose separate leaflets unfold.
stages.title: Leaf expansion

stages.text: Successive shoots and branches enlarge the tree's leaf-bearing framework.
stages.title: Canopy building

stages.text: Flowers form at leaf axils and can develop into smooth seed capsules.
stages.title: Reproductive growth

habitat.text: Pachira glabra comes from southeastern and southern Brazil and grows in the wet tropical biome. Its leafy tree form brings a different growth pattern to this collection: an expanding woody framework carries an open canopy of compound leaves, rather than a compact water-storing cactus body.

Subject: a young unbraided Pachira money tree, working identification Pachira cf. glabra. Show a single smooth green-brown upright trunk and an open canopy of palmately compound leaves, each with five to seven separate glossy elongated leaflets meeting at the end of one long petiole. Warm ivory background; accurate clean pen-and-watercolor, forest-green/sage/ochre palette, generous whitespace, large central specimen. Show exactly four bold legible circular numbered markers 1, 2, 3, 4 and thin clear leader lines, with no other text: 1 points into one individual leaflet blade; 2 points to the shared junction where the leaflets of one compound leaf meet; 3 points to the long petiole below that junction; 4 points to the smooth trunk. Keep number-marker endpoints unambiguous, legible at 350px width. No flowers, fruit, roots, braided stems, grafts, title, paragraphs, watering icons, calendar, pot, or decorative objects. This is a general botanical structural illustration, not a portrait or identification proof of a specific owned plant.

lookalikes.name: Pachira aquatica
lookalikes.text: The Florida flora key distinguishes P. aquatica by red-tipped stamens and rough brown fruit. P. glabra has white stamens and smooth green fruit; these reproductive details are more useful than the shared money-tree name.

mature.text: Flora Zambesiaca describes a 3–5 m tree with compound leaves on stalks reaching about 15 cm. Leaflets spread from a shared point, giving the canopy its open, hand-shaped outline.

nameStory.text: Kew traces the accepted P. glabra name to an 1868 publication and includes older descriptions under Bombacopsis glabra and Bombax oleagineum. Those historical names help explain why reference sources can look inconsistent.
